memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"'I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of Egypt so that you would
no longer be slaves to the Egyptians; I broke the bars of your yoke and
enabled you to walk with heads held high'" - Lev 26:13 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God signs off the section of blessings by pointing back to the exodus. I
broke the bars of your yoke, He says, and enabled you to walk with heads
held high. A yoke was the wooden bar laid across the neck of an animal or
a slave. God had shattered it.

Picture the change. Slaves walk bent, eyes down, shoulders bowed under
the weight of bondage and shame. Freed people walk upright, heads lifted,
able to look the world in the eye. God had transformed His people from
the first into the second.

Dear friend, this is a beautiful picture of what God does for those He
redeems. Sin bends us low. Guilt makes us walk with our eyes down. Shame
tells us to keep our heads bowed. But God breaks the yoke.

Paul writes that it is for freedom that Christ has set us free, and urges
us not to submit again to a yoke of slavery (Gal 5:1). Jesus said, come to
me, and I will give you rest; take my yoke, for it is easy and my burden
is light (Matt 11:28-30) — trading the crushing yoke of bondage for the
gentle yoke of belonging to Him.

If you have been walking bent under guilt or shame, hear this. Your yoke
has been broken at the cross. You are no longer a slave. Lift your head.
Walk upright. You are a redeemed and beloved child of God.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Am I still walking bent under guilt or shame Christ has removed?
2. What "yoke" has God broken in my life?
3. How would walking with my head held high, as a freed child, look
   today?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, thank You for breaking the yoke of my bondage in Christ. Lift my
head, free me from shame, and help me walk upright as Your redeemed child.
Amen.
